Shri Sanjay Kumar Sharma - Advocate for L.Rs of respo
 Order

This miscellaneous appeal under Section 30 of the Employee Compensation Act has been preferred against the impugned award dated 02.02.2022 in Case No.64/WC/2010(NF) whereby an award of Rs.3,00,846/- with interest @12% per annum has been awarded from one month after the date of incident i.e. 15.07.2009 along with medical expenses of Rs.10,660/-
2.
The brief facts of the case are that respondent no.1-claimant (now deceased) was engaged as driver on bus bearing number MP-09-FA-2151 under the employment of respondent no.2.
On 15.07.2009 he was tying Tripal on the roof of the bus suddenly monkey attacked him and he fell down and sustained injuries.

The aforesaid claim petition was filed under the Workmen Compensation Act, 1923 (for short hereinafter referred to as "Act") claiming compensation of Rs.3,67,416/- on account of death of the injured in the said accident.
The bus was insured under the Motor Vehicles NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3850 2 MA-1857-2022 Act, 1988 with the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: The appellant filed the written statement before the Commissioner and raised objections therein and also examined RTO Officer Bhaiyalal (DW-1) and Company Officer Shivani (DW-2) to prove the defence.

After framing issues and recording evidence, the objections raised on behalf of the Insurance Company were rejected and the impugned award was passed for the amount mentioned herein above which is under challenge in this miscellaneous appeal.
3. Counsel for the appellant submits that the deceased Virendrasingh did not suffer injuries in the course of employment.
The respondent no.1 failed to adduce any documentary evidence about the employment as a paid driver in the insured vehicle.
Giving this finding, the learned Commissioner has fell in error.
Fake imployment was pleaded in order to get the compensation amount under the provisions of the Act.

Since respondent no.1 now deceased was pleaded as driver on the bus,

sentences.text: Learned Commissioner committed error in interpreting the terms and condition of the insurance policy issued under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicle Act and held Insurance Company liable to pay compensation.
Insurance Company was not liable to pay compensation, as there was breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy Ex.D-2.
There was breach of permit as bus whereon respondent no.1 was employed was not having permit and could have been plied without permit and fitness.

Due to this breach which is in contravention of Section 66 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the Insurance Company cannot be NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3850 3 MA-1857-2022 fastened with the liability to pay compensation.

3.1 He further submits that the learned Commissioner has committed error in holding that the respondent no.1 has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 100% and also loss of earning capacity to the extent of 100%., whereas permanent disability certificate given by the doctor mentions disability to the extent of 36% only.
He further submits that medical expenses were not permissible under the Act for permanent disablement.
It is only permissible for partial disablement.
Section 4(2)(2A) of the Act was not applicable when the accident took place on 15.07.2009 and the aforesaid Act came into force on 18.01.2010.
Hence, learned commissioner committed error of law in allowing medical expenses to claimant by giving the effect of amendment retrospectively.
As per Section 4-A of the Act it is only the employer who is made liable for payment of penalty, therefore, is also liable to pay interest and not the Insurance Company.
On these submissions prays for allowing this appeal by setting aside the impugned award.

He has relied upon the judgments in the case of Neelam Devi and others Vs. Devendra Singh Yadav and another 2006 ACJ 139 (para 9), Pal Raj Vs.
Divisional Controller, North East Karnataka Road Transport Corporation 2010 ACJ 2859 (paras 11,13,14), National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Mubasir Ahmad 2007 AIR SCW 1265 (para 8),
National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Challa Bharathamma and others, 2004 ACJ 2094 (paras 12, 13).
4.

sentences.text: Per contra, counsel for the respondent no.1 submits that no illegality has been committed by the learned Commissioner for payment of award amount along with interest.

He further submits that owner of the bus NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3850 4 MA-1857-2022 has admitted that respondent no.1 was in employment on his bus and accident occurred during the course of employment.
In view of the aforesaid admission, no further evidence was required to prove that the respondent no.1 was in employment.

Even otherwise, appropriate evidence has been led before the learned Commissioner and that has been appreciated in right perspective and amount has been awarded by applying the formula available for computing the compensation amount.

Relying upon para 6 of the judgment of the Delhi High Court in the case of Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs.
Babu and another 2014 DHC 1508 he submits that no illegality has been committed in allowing the medial expenses also.

sentences.text: 6. From perusal of the written statement file by the owner of the bus it is apparent that respondent no.1 deceased was working as driver on the bus bearing number MP-09-FA-2151 on the date of accident i.e. 15.07.2009.
Even otherwise, Virendrasingh-respondent no.1 deceased as deposed that he was in the employment of bus bearing number MP-09-FA-2151 as driver on the date of incident.
The incident took place when he was tying Tripal on the roof of the bus when he was attacked by monkey and fell down and suffered grievous injuries in the lumbar region by fracture of bone.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident, he has suffered disablement and he cannot perform his duties as driver.
Rahul has also been examined on behalf of the respondent and he has also proved the fact of incident and injuries suffered by the respondent no.1. during the course of employment.

Therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3850 5 MA-1857-2022 argument advanced on behalf of the Insurance Company that respondent no.1 was not in the employment when the accident took place cannot be accepted.

7. Dr. Ashish Jain (AW-3) has deposed before the Court that he examined the respondent no.1 who suffered injuries in the accident occurred on 15.07.2009 as he fell down from the bus and suffered fracture in right hip bone and he was operated and screw and plates were implanted.
He also suffered fracture in the right wrist and thereby incurred disablement of 28% in lower limb and 8% in the right upper limb.

This Court cannot be oblivious of this fact that if driver suffers injury, fracture of right hip bone and fracture in the right wrist, his functional disability comes to 100% as far as his driving work is concerned.
Therefore, no fault can be found with in the findings given by the learned Commissioner in this regard.
At the time of accident bus was stationary.

It was not being plied on the road therefore, assuming that there was no permit at the time, it will not help the Insurance Company in getting exonerated from paying the awarded amount to the employee.

8. Taking income of the deceased as Rs.3,800/- and applying the formula given for computing the compensation amount Rs.3,00,846/- has been assessed as amount to be paid to the claimant and Rs.10,660/- as medical expenses has been allowed.
Payment of medical expenses appears against the Act.

Therefore the contention of the appellant that medical expenses were not permissible under Section 4(2)(2A) of the Act as the accident took place on 15.07.2009 and the Act came into force on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3850 6 MA-1857-2022 18.01.2010 is accepted and the medical expenses allowed by the learned Commissioner by giving the effect of amendment retrospectively cannot be granted.

9. In the case of Neelam Devi (Supra) the Insurance Company was exonerated on the ground that driving licence has not been produced and evidence to demonstrate that employee was under employment was not proved, but this is not a case here, therefore the judgment is not of any help to the Insurance Company.
For the same reasons case of Pal Raj (Supra) is also of no help.

Similarly,
the case of Mubasir Ahmed (Supra) is also of no help as with regard to the injuries sustained and disability, there is ample evidence on record to show that deceased was driver and suffered disablement in right leg and also in right wrist.

The case of Challa Bharathamma and others (Supra)
permits defence to the Insurance Company as there was no permit for plying the vehicle, but in this case, as mentioned herein above, the bus was not being plied at the time of accident, therefore breach of permit if any could not exonerate the Insurance Company from the liability.
Hence, these judgments do not come to the rescue of the Insurance Company.
